content.title: Pacific Crest Trail Hikers Incorporate Joshua Tree National Park Detours
content.text: Published Apr 14, 2026 - 08:56 11 Reads Last Update Apr 14, 2026 - 08:56 I had always wanted to visit to see George Washington’s alleged initials on the bridge at Natural Bridge State Park in Virginia.Hiking & Camping Smallest Font Largest Font Outdoor enthusiasts completing the southern sections of the Pacific Crest Trail (PCT) are increasingly incorporating Joshua Tree National Park into their itineraries as an unconventional "side quest." On April 12, 2026, reports from the hiking community highlighted how travelers are leveraging the park's proximity to Palm Springs to visit iconic desert landmarks after finishing their trail miles.The detour typically follows the completion of the first 151 miles of the PCT, which ends near Paradise Valley Cafe in Southern California. Hikers are utilizing local transportation and rental cars from Palm Springs International Airport to reach the national park, located approximately one hour away from the city. "Visiting all of the national parks in the U.S. has been a dream of mine for quite some time now," stated a section hiker in a report by thetrek.co. The hiker noted that while the PCT passes through seven national parks, Joshua Tree remains a popular external addition due to its unique geological features.Regional Parks & Gardens Visitors to the park focus on short-distance excursions to accommodate post-trail fatigue. Key points of interest include the Hall of Horrors, known for its dense concentration of Joshua trees, and various rock formations such as Arch Rock, Heart Rock, and Skull Rock. Many travelers arrive before sunrise at the Twentynine Palms entrance to avoid heavy mid-day crowds. In addition to sightseeing, the park serves as a vantage point for upcoming trail challenges. From the Keys View overlook, hikers can observe the Coachella Valley along with Mt. San Jacinto and San Gorgonio, which represent the next major elevation gains on the northbound PCT route.While the park is a global destination for bouldering and rock climbing, most trail hikers opt for sightseeing due to a lack of specialized technical gear. Standard visits often include stops at Split Rock and panoramic views of the high desert landscape before returning to Palm Springs for departure flights. 0 Like 0 Dislike 0 Funny 0 Angry 0 Sad 0 Wow
